FQ-189 — Meera Iyer (VP of Finance, CFO's Office)

Two last things for this ticket. First — I'm told there's an EFS filesystem in the cost breakdown attached to something that only ever runs on one server, which doesn't sound right to me even without the technical details. Second — I want that growing bucket resolved this time, not just narrowed further. We've spent five lessons on storage; let's close this properly.

Meera Iyer — VP of Finance, CFO's Office

So it was sitting in a region nobody actually looks at day to day — a compliance export that made sense three years ago, running quietly ever since, for a requirement that doesn't even apply anymore. That's the real pattern across this whole ticket, isn't it — not carelessness, just nobody's job to notice. I'm glad it's finally closed, and I'm glad you didn't just delete three years of exported data without checking what it actually was first.

That's storage done, and honestly, that's this ticket done. From a s3fs-mounted log script to a lifecycle rule that broke real images to a compliance export nobody remembered — every piece of this had a real, findable reason, and now every piece has an actual owner. Thank you for treating my finance questions like real engineering questions.

Ravi mentioned monitoring is next — I have a feeling we're going to find out how much of this was already visible somewhere, if anyone had been looking.

— Meera

tasks.question: What makes S3 Glacier Vault Lock different from regular S3 lifecycle policies moving data to Glacier?
options: A) There's no real difference — Vault Lock is just a different name for the same Glacier storage class

D) Vault Lock automatically deletes data after the retention period, while regular Glacier keeps it forever

Checking the function's own code and an old internal doc found alongside it reveals it was set up roughly 3 years ago to satisfy a data export requirement for a compliance framework FoodQuick was pursuing at the time — a requirement that was later superseded by a different, newer process (confirmed with the compliance team), but this specific Lambda and its nightly schedule were never turned off.
tasks.fix: Confirm with the compliance team that this specific export is genuinely no longer required (done). Disable the EventBridge schedule triggering the Lambda, then delete the Lambda function and revoke legacy-export-service-role's permissions. Before deleting the 340GB of already-exported data, have compliance/legal confirm no retention obligation applies to the historical exports themselves, separate from the now-obsolete ongoing export process.

correct_answers.case_1: EFS — genuine multi-instance concurrent shared access is exactly EFS's purpose, worth the cost premium here

correct_answers.case_4: S3 with a standard lifecycle policy (e.g. to IA or Glacier over time) — retention without needing the strict, hard-to-undo immutability of Vault Lock
